commands.name: describe-image
commands.description: Describe what an image shows, concretely and in reading order.
commands.body:
# Describe Image

Describe what the selected image shows, in the order a reader would notice it. Name concrete elements — labels, values, controls, people, layout — rather than summarising the impression. Say plainly when something is unreadable rather than guessing at it.

commands.name: explain-code
commands.description: Explain the selected code for someone new to the codebase.
commands.body:
# Explain Code

Explain the selected code for an engineer who is new to this codebase. Cover what it does, how it is used, and what it depends on. Reference concrete file and symbol names.

commands.name: extract-text
commands.description: Transcribe every piece of text visible in an image.
commands.body:
# Extract Text

Transcribe every piece of text visible in the selected image, preserving its reading order and grouping. Keep labels with their values. Mark anything you cannot read confidently as [unclear] instead of inventing it.

commands.name: read-chart
commands.description: Read a chart or diagram and report what its data says.
commands.body:
# Read Chart

Read the selected chart or diagram. State what is being measured, over what range, and what the data actually says — including the trend and any outlier. Quote axis labels and units verbatim, and say when a value can only be estimated from the image.

commands.name: release-notes
commands.description: Turn the selected sources into user-facing release notes.
commands.body:
# Release Notes

Write release notes from the selected sources. Group changes under Added, Changed, and Fixed. Write each entry for a user of the product, not for its authors.

commands.name: ship-it
commands.description: A release checklist prompt that walks through pre-ship verification steps.
commands.body:
# Ship It

Run this checklist before shipping a change:

1. **Tests** — run the project's test suite; confirm it passes.
2. **Lint/format** — run the project's linter/formatter; confirm zero warnings.
3. **Diff review** — re-read the full diff for anything unintended (debug
   prints, commented-out code, secrets).
4. **Changelog/docs** — update if user-facing behavior changed.
5. **Commit** — one logical change per commit, clear message.

commands.name: summarize
commands.description: Summarise the selected sources, most important point first.
commands.body:
# Summarize

Summarize the selected sources. Lead with the single most important point, then give the supporting detail as short bullets. Omit anything the sources do not state.
